items.title: Why SAP screens every AI project for ethical and environmental risks
items.summary: SAP isn’t the only enterprise software company with an official artificial intelligence ethics policy, but it’s one of the few that have included explicit criteria covering environmental considerations.

items.title: Shareholders continue to pull back on environmental resolutions
items.summary: The number of shareholder resolutions focused on environmental issues continues to decline, according to a review of proposals filed during the first half of 2026.

items.title: Could mortgage lenders help households adapt to heatwaves?
items.summary: As research finds that heatwaves could cost the UK £25.6bn in losses each year by 2030, the UK Sustainable Investment and Finance Association has claimed that green mortgages could be expanded to help households adapt to climate risks.

items.title: Only a minority of UK wants EV transition to slow down, poll finds
items.summary: Research by charging industry association ChargeUK and YouGov has found only a minority of people in the UK think the Government should slow down the electric vehicle (EV) transition.

items.title: From Scope 3 to packaging reforms: edie’s next virtual collaborations open to Members
items.summary: From September to December, edie is hosting bi-weekly virtual discussions on a host of key topics to help sustainability professionals upskill departments, learn from other sectors and promote sustainable actions.

items.title: Fossil fuel gains outweigh AI’s climate benefits, study finds
items.summary: According to new analysis, fossil fuel productivity gains enabled by artificial intelligence (AI) will outweigh any emissions reductions the technology generates across renewable energy applications – a huge carbon reporting blind spot.

items.title: Homes near pylon projects to receive discounted energy bills under Government scheme
items.summary: The Government is offering cheaper energy bills for communities that host grid infrastructure, with savings of up to £2,500 expected over the next 10 years.

items.title: Analysis: Weaker EV targets could cost UK consumers £3bn a year by 2030
items.summary: An upcoming UK government consultation on weakening targets for electric vehicles (EVs) could cost consumers as much as £3bn a year by 2030, according to Carbon Brief analysis.

海保救援網首次成功救援革龜、韓企進軍海上AI資料中心計畫、阿曼海洋保護區油輪漏油
